claim_text: Tumour NK dysfunction reversible vs fixed

audit.primary_source_citation: Pouxvielh K, Marotel M, Drouillard A, Villard M, Moreews M, ... Fournier A, Thaunat O, Marçais A, Walzer T. "Tumor-induced natural killer cell dysfunction is a rapid and reversible process uncoupled from the expression of immune checkpoints." Sci Adv. 2024 Aug 28;10(35):eadn0164. doi:10.1126/sciadv.adn0164. PMID 39196934 / PMC11352832. Archived: /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PMC11352832.txt. STRONGEST COUNTER-SOURCE (the "fixed" arm): Schmid K, Haimerl C, Stark J, ... Böttcher JP, Schmid RM, Wiedemann GM. "Prolonged TGF-β locks NK cells in a dysfunctional state through persistent epigenetic remodeling of IRF, T-bet and EOMES binding sites." bioRxiv 2026-02-14, doi:10.64898/2026.02.11.705354, Europe PMC PPR1223917 — NOT PEER-REVIEWED (biorxiv API "published":"NA" as of 2026-08-14). Archived: /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PPR1223917.txt. Third source read in full: Nat Commun 2024;15:682, PMID 38267402 / PMC10808449, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PMC10808449.txt.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Primary source (Sci Adv 2024) and counter-source (bioRxiv PPR1223917, retrieved via Europe PMC fullTextXML after biorxiv.org returned HTTP 403/500) were both read in full at the Methods level. Two secondary JCI papers checked (Ardolino 2014 PMID 25329698; Merino 2019 PMID 31211698) returned ABSTRACT_ONLY through lit.py because JCI is not in the Europe PMC OA subset; Ardolino's Methods were recovered separately via PMC4347250. Figure-legend n values for the primary source's key reversal panels were recovered from the PMC HTML, since lit.py's strip_xml() deletes <fig> blocks.
audit.species: Primary source: mouse (C57BL/6J; congenic Ly5a x C57BL/6J for CD45.1/CD45.2 discrimination; Prf1-/- in supporting arms). Counter-source: human (healthy adult volunteer PBMC-derived NK cells for the in vitro arm; HCC / liver-metastasis patients for the ex vivo arm).
audit.what_was_measured: In C57BL/6J mice injected i.v. with 5x10^7 RMA-KR lymphoma cells (RMA CRISPR-edited to B2m-KO and lentivirally transduced with the NKG2D ligand Rae1-beta, i.e. an MHC-I-negative, NK-activating disseminated lymphoma), at late-stage tumour growth, splenic NK cells were FACS-sorted and adoptively transferred via the retro-orbital sinus into tumour-free congenic Ly5a x C57BL/6J recipients; 7 to 13 days after transfer donor-derived NK cells were re-purified from recipients (donor vs recipient discriminated by CD45.2 versus CD45.1-CD45.2 alleles) and assayed by flow cytometry for (a) surface Lag-3, CD73 and Tim-3 and (b) co-expression of CD107a and IFN-gamma after plate-bound anti-NK1.1 crosslinking or cytokine restimulation, in n = 10 to 15 mice per group (n = 3 to 12 for the ICP heatmap panel). In the same study, in vitro, NK cells sorted from RMA-KR-bearing mice at late-stage tumour growth were cultured with IL-15 or IL-21 and assayed for viability and for CD107a/IFN-gamma after NK1.1 stimulation, in n = 3 to 18 mice per group; and in vivo, RMA-KR-bearing mice received 2 doses of 4 ug IL-15/IL-15Ralpha complex i.p. 2 days apart with NK function assayed the day after the second dose. In the counter-source, human NK cells enriched from healthy-donor PBMC were cultured in IL-15 (50 ng/mL) +/- TGF-beta (10 ng/mL) for short-term versus a 17-day prolonged setup, TGF-beta was withdrawn by a single PBS wash into fresh medium, and chromatin accessibility (bulk ATAC-seq), transcription (bulk RNA-seq, 5 biological replicates per condition), H3K4me3/H3K27ac/CTCF occupancy (CUT&RUN, 250,000-500,000 sorted cells per reaction) and killing of BxPC-3 PDAC targets (xCELLigence impedance, 1:1 E:T, 48 h) were measured after withdrawal.
audit.n: Primary source, key reversal-by-transfer experiment: n = 10 to 15 mice per group (function panel), n = 3 to 12 mice per group (ICP panel). Primary source, in vitro cytokine rescue of sorted dysfunctional NK cells: n = 3 to 18 mice per group. Counter-source: 5 biological replicates (healthy donors) per condition for RNA-seq; donor/patient numbers for ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN and the HCC cohort are not stated numerically anywhere in the preprint Methods (killing assay stated only as "at least duplicate").
audit.n_unit: mice (primary source; NOT cells — sorted NK pools were per-mouse and group sizes are stated per mouse in the figure legends); donors/patients (counter-source)
audit.controls: Primary source: (i) tumour-free control-mouse NK cells sorted and transferred in parallel through the identical pipeline; (ii) a second tumour arm, parental RMA (MHC-I+, non-NK-activating), which induced ICPs but NOT dysfunction — this dissociates tumour burden from dysfunction; (iii) pre-transfer baseline measured on the same sorted populations ("analyzed before and after transfer"); (iv) an explicit anti-selection control — frequency of NK cells recovered from the RMA-KR condition was compared with control and reported as "in the same order of magnitude" (fig. S7C); (v) depletion/blockade specificity controls (200 ug polyclonal anti-rat IgG isotype; depletion confirmed with antibody clones different from those used to deplete); (vi) IgG2a isotype for plate-bound stimulation. Stated methodological weaknesses, verbatim: "The number of mice used in each experiment was not power-calculated, given the large number of questions asked"; "No randomization was performed, with the exception of experiments in which animal survival was monitored"; "data from mice in which tumors had not grown were excluded." Counter-source controls: IL-15-only cultures matched for time, and continuous-TGF-beta versus withdrawal arms; the authors themselves flag the confound that "NK cells were maintained in IL-15 for prolonged culture periods, and long-term IL-15 exposure itself has been reported to induce transcriptional and epigenetic adaptations."
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION, NOT PER-CELL REVERSION. Over the 7-13 days the sorted NK cells spend in the tumour-free congenic host, a residual functional minority could preferentially survive and/or proliferate (the host is IL-15-replete and NK turnover is fast on that timescale), so the recovered CD45.2 population need not be the same cells that were dysfunctional at sort. The paper's only guard against this is a frequency argument — recovered NK numbers were "in the same order of magnitude" as control (fig. S7C) — with no proliferation dye in that particular experiment (CTV was used in the transfer-INTO-tumour experiments, not the transfer-OUT-of-tumour recovery experiment), no clonal or per-cell tracking, and no barcoding. SECOND, AND MORE IMPORTANT FOR THE CLAIM AS WORDED: the lesion this paper demonstrates and then reverses is a proximal-signalling one — impaired Akt/Erk/S6 phosphorylation with normal STAT5, and reduced CD122 internalisation, i.e. an mTORC1-level defect — and a signalling-level state is close to definitionally reversible once the engaging ligand is withdrawn. The study performs NO chromatin, methylation or ATAC readout at any point, so it cannot exclude a stable epigenetic program at effector loci coexisting with recovered CD107a/IFN-gamma. THIRD, SCOPE: RMA-KR is a disseminated MHC-I-null lymphoma read out in spleen; the "dysfunctional" cells are splenic NK cells from a tumour-bearing animal, not NK cells dissected out of a solid-tumour mass, so generalisation to the solid-tumour TME that the R2 wording invokes is an extrapolation. For the counter-source, the mirror-image alternative is that 17 days of continuous high-dose IL-15 plus TGF-beta in a 96-well plate drives terminal differentiation/senescence or culture exhaustion, and that the HCC ATAC signal is measured on PERIPHERAL BLOOD NK cells cross-sectionally, which cannot distinguish an imprint acquired in the tumour and carried out of it from a systemic effect on NK cells that never entered the tumour, or from a shift in CD56bright/CD56dim composition between patients and controls.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it materially changes the picture. (1) Schmid/Wiedemann, bioRxiv 2026-02-14 (PPR1223917) is the single strongest "fixed" source and directly contradicts unrestricted reversibility: short-term TGF-beta gives largely reversible transcriptional/accessibility change, but a 17-day exposure produces suppression of cytotoxicity and cytokine production that "persists even after signal withdrawal," with persistently closed regions enriched for IRF, EOMES and T-BET motifs and loss of H3K4me3 at effector promoters — and, critically, that state is "refractory to diverse reactivation cues, including pro-inflammatory cytokines and activating receptor engagement," i.e. it explicitly resists the IL-15/IL-12/IL-18/anti-NKp46 rescue that the reversible-side literature relies on. It is however NOT peer-reviewed, and its irreversibility demonstration is entirely in vitro on healthy-donor NK cells with recombinant TGF-beta; no tumour-derived NK cell is ever subjected to a withdrawal experiment. (2) Within the primary source itself there is internal counter-evidence to naive reversibility: "Ex vivo blockade of ICPs in cultures of total splenocytes from RMA-KR-bearing mice did not restore NK cell responsiveness, even when several ICPs were targeted," and in vivo Tim-3 or Lag-3 blockade improved neither survival nor NK function; and high-dose IL-15 in vitro improved but did not fully normalise dysfunctional NK reactivity ("a difference with control NK cells persisted, suggesting that other signals were necessary to fully revert dysfunction"). (3) Nat Commun 2024 (PMID 38267402), which tracked NK fate in MC38/CT26/B16 tumours with Kaede photoconversion, shows IL-15:IL-15Ra PREVENTS loss of function but names reversal as untested, verbatim: "Future studies of how changes in NK cell function are regulated should also consider whether the conversion of cNK to a tumor-retained state is reversible and the extent to which epigenetic changes underpin this transition." (4) Ardolino 2014 JCI (PMID 25329698) supports the reversible side in vivo but only for MHC-I-deficient tumours (IL-12+IL-18 100 ng each i.p. every other day, or 20 ug H9 IL-2 superkine, from day 7 for 4 weeks, at least 4-5 mice per group), and was ineffective in MHC-I+ tumours — so even the reversible side is conditional on tumour genotype.
audit.downstream_dependency: Two named dependencies inside this screen. (1) CLAIM R3 ("After TGF-beta withdrawal residency reverts, effector function does not", graded OBSERVATION (Schmid/Wiedemann, ATAC) in /home/user/aaa/phaseA/claims.json) resolves to the SAME document that is R2's only strong "fixed" source — bioRxiv PPR1223917. R3 is therefore not independent corroboration of R2's fixed arm; both stand or fall on one unrefereed preprint, and any Phase-C weighting that treats R2-fixed and R3 as two converging lines of evidence is double-counting a single dataset. (2) CLAIM X5 ("NK -> exhausted NK", flagged WEAKEST: the end state itself is undefined") depends on R2 directly: if tumour NK dysfunction is the proximal-signalling, transfer-reversible state that PMID 39196934 demonstrates, then "exhausted NK" is not a differentiation endpoint and X5 has no terminus to trace to. Secondarily, R2's resolution constrains T4 ("NK -> ILC1 within tumours") and X2, because the Nat Commun 2024 CD49a+ "tumour-retained" state is the same population both claims argue over.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's initial call was "HEAVILY OCCUPIED ALREADY". That is a factual claim about the literature, and it is half right in a way that would misdirect prioritisation if taken at face value. The REVERSIBLE arm is indeed heavily occupied and has genuinely strong primary work: in vivo mouse congenic adoptive transfer out of a tumour-bearing host with functional recovery (PMID 39196934, n = 10-15 mice/group), in vivo cytokine reversal of NK anergy in MHC-I-deficient tumours (PMID 25329698), and IL-15-mediated prevention of intratumoural function loss with photoconversion fate-tracking (PMID 38267402). The FIXED arm is NOT heavily occupied. Across 9 lit.py searches and 5 web searches I found no peer-reviewed primary study that takes tumour-derived NK cells, removes them from the tumour signal, and shows with a chromatin or methylation readout that dysfunction fails to revert. The strongest fixed-side evidence in existence as of 2026-08-14 is a Feb-2026 bioRxiv preprint (PPR1223917) that is (a) not peer-reviewed, (b) in vitro on healthy-donor NK cells with recombinant TGF-beta rather than tumour NK cells, and (c) whose only in vivo human arm is cross-sectional ATAC on PERIPHERAL BLOOD NK cells from HCC patients, which is INF_MARKER and cannot establish irreversibility. A 2024 primary paper states in print that the question is open. So the correct occupancy statement is asymmetric: "the restoration/cytokine side is saturated; the load-bearing comparator — durable epigenetic fixation in tumour NK cells — rests on one unrefereed in vitro preprint." Recording R2 as uniformly "heavily occupied" would license skipping the one sub-question that is actually thin. NOT overturned: the claim remains, correctly, out of the lineage-screen core (see is_lineage_claim), and nothing here justifies raising its priority above the tumour-lineage claims X1/X2.
audit.methods_quote: Primary source, verbatim (Sci Adv 2024, "Adoptive transfer of NK cells to assess functional recovery"): "NK cells from control or RMA-KR-bearing mice were FACS-sorted and adoptively transferred into Ly5a x C57BL/6J mice via the retro-orbital sinus. After 7 to 13 days, NK cells were purified from recipient mice and their phenotype and functionality were assessed. Transferred NK cells were distinguished from recipient NK cells based on CD45 alleles (CD45.2 versus CD45.1-CD45.2)." Study-design caveat, verbatim: "The number of mice used in each experiment was not power-calculated, given the large number of questions asked... No randomization was performed, with the exception of experiments in which animal survival was monitored... In each experiment with tumor-bearing mice, data from mice in which tumors had not grown were excluded." Counter-source, verbatim (bioRxiv PPR1223917, "Cultivation of NK cells"): "In general, they were either cultured with IL-15 (50 ng/mL, Miltenyi) alone or in combination with IL-15 and TGF-beta (10 ng/mL, R&D) in IMDM+ at 37C, 5% CO2. In cases where TGF-beta was withdrawn, cells were transferred to a low-bind tube, washed once with PBS, resuspended in fresh media, and transferred to a new well... For the 17-day setup, cells were neither handled nor supplemented between days 0-7 and 7-17." Counter-source patient arm, verbatim: "Blood from HCC patients was obtained from the HCC outpatient clinic... Blood NK cells were isolated as described above and cultured overnight in IMDM+ medium supplemented with 10 ng/mL hIL-15 and 25 U/mL IL-2."

audit.notes: IS THIS A LINEAGE CLAIM? NO — and this is the decisive point for the later phase. R2 as worded ("Tumour NK dysfunction is reversible versus fixed") is a FUNCTIONAL/STATE claim: can the effector capacity of a cell be restored once suppressed. It is not of the form "does A give rise to B". Nothing in the primary source is a claim about ancestry: the CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic transfer is used to prove that THE SAME transferred cells regained CD107a/IFN-gamma output, not that one NK population is the progenitor of another. Same for the counter-source, which asks only whether a suppressed chromatin state at effector loci persists after the suppressing ligand is washed out. It belongs with R1 ("dNK -> cytotoxic (IL-15/IL-18 rescue)", already flagged FUNCTIONAL, NOT LINEAGE) and R3, not with D1-D4/P1-P3/X1-X5. CAVEAT ON THE BOUNDARY, stated so the later phase is not misled: the literature that answers R2 is entangled with a genuine state-transition claim, because Nat Commun 2024 (PMID 38267402) frames the same biology as circulating CD49b+CD11b+ cNK cells entering the tumour and becoming a CD49a+ "tumour-retained" state — that IS a directional state-transition claim and it is the substance of X2/T4. So R2's evidence base can be mined for X2/T4, but R2 itself should not be scored on the lineage rubric. NO OPINION IS OFFERED HERE ON WHETHER R2 IS WORTH PURSUING. WHY THE PRIMARY SOURCE IS PMID 39196934 AND NOT ARDOLINO 2014: both are in vivo mouse, but Ardolino tests whether exogenous cytokine restores function while tumour is still present (a therapeutic-response readout that cannot separate reinvigoration of dysfunctional cells from priming of not-yet-dysfunctional ones — a confound Ardolino's own field acknowledges and which the Sci Adv introduction names explicitly), whereas PMID 39196934 removes the cells from the tumour host entirely and tracks the identical congenically-marked population, which is the only design in the peer-reviewed literature I found that directly interrogates reversibility per se. EVIDENCE-TYPE ATTRIBUTION (G2/G7 discipline): OBS_TRANSFER = the congenic sort-and-transfer recovery experiment in PMID 39196934, the strongest single item and the basis of the row's classification. INF_KINETIC = the 16 h / 72 h / 168 h transfer-in timing series used to argue dysfunction precedes ICP induction — timing, not observation of a transition. INF_INVITRO = sorted-NK + IL-15/IL-21 rescue cultures and ex vivo ICP blockade (PMID 39196934), and the entire withdrawal/ATAC/CUT&RUN programme of the counter-source preprint. INF_MARKER = surface ICP and CD103 phenotyping, and the cross-sectional HCC blood-NK ATAC comparison. INF_TRAJECTORY = PAGA + diffusion pseudotime in PMID 38267402, rooted by hand in the Kaede-green cluster; per G2 this is inference and is listed last, and no part of this row's grading rests on it. I did NOT list OBS_GENETIC: the CRISPR B2m knockout in PMID 39196934 is applied to the TUMOUR line and Prf1-/- is a functional knockout, so neither is genetic fate-mapping of NK cells; calling it OBS_GENETIC would be exactly the loosening G7 forbids. OCCUPANCY, AS A FACTUAL STATEMENT: the reversible arm is saturated (cytokine and checkpoint restoration studies across two decades, multiple species, multiple tumour models); the fixed arm has, to the limit of the 19 searches logged, exactly one strong dedicated primary study and it is an unrefereed in vitro preprint. Per G3 I record this as searched-and-not-found, not as non-existence. adv.challenge_reason: OBS_TRANSFER survives as the strongest class, but the row overstates what it licenses and misses a G5 defect. VERIFIED IN THE METHODS MYSELF (/home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PMC11352832.txt line 133): "NK cells from control or RMA-KR-bearing mice were FACS-sorted and adoptively transferred into Ly5a x C57BL/6J mice via the retro-orbital sinus. After 7 to 13 days, NK cells were purified from recipient mice... distinguished from recipient NK cells based on CD45 alleles (CD45.2 versus CD45.1-CD45.2)." That is a genuine congenically marked adoptive transfer read out on the donor-derived population, so downgrading it to INF_MARKER would misdescribe the method — G7 forbids loosening but equally forbids manufacturing severity. I independently recovered the Fig. 7 legend from the PMC HTML and CONFIRM the auditor's two contested items: the phrase "They were analyzed before and after transfer" is real (it is in the Fig. 7 legend, not the Methods, which is why it is absent from the stripped archive), and n = 10 to 15 mice per group (CD107a/IFN-g) and n = 3 to 12 (ICP) are correct. Credit where due. WHAT THE ROW GETS WRONG. (1) SCOPE. OBS_TRANSFER here observes only "donor-derived NK cells recovered from a tumour-free host are functional at day 7-13." The claim R2 actually asserts - that the cells which were dysfunctional reverted - is not observed. No cell is assayed twice; "before" is an aliquot of the sorted donor pool, "after" is cells harvested from different (recipient) animals. The bridge between the two is carried entirely by fig. S7C, whose full argument is: "This was unlikely due to the selection of a small functional population because the frequency of NK cells recovered from the RMA-KR condition was in the same order of magnitude as that of the control condition." That is a population-frequency comparison BETWEEN DIFFERENT RECIPIENT MICE credited as evidence that the same cells persisted - precisely the pattern flagged in the re-examination brief, and it is INF_KINETIC/INF_MARKER grade, not observation grade. "Same order of magnitude" also tolerates a ~5-fold loss, and a frequency argument is structurally blind to the scenario that matters (minority survives and proliferates to refill the niche). (2) G5 DEFECT THE ROW ASSERTS AWAY. The row states n_unit as "mice... sorted NK pools were per-mouse and group sizes are stated per mouse in the figure legends." The legend does NOT say that. I checked the legend explicitly for pooling and it is silent. n = 10-15 counts RECIPIENT mice; the independent unit for a tumour-induced-dysfunction claim is the DONOR (tumour-bearing) mouse. End-stage RMA-KR donors are NK-poor by the paper's own data (fig. S2, B and C: "the number of mature NK cells dropped during tumor progression"), and the study's other transfers used 1 x 10^6 NK cells per recipient, so supplying 10-15 recipients almost certainly required pooling donors. Effective donor-level n is therefore unreported and plausibly single-digit or n = 1 pool. The row converted an unstated design detail into a rigour claim. (3) UNMEASURED DIVISION. CTV was used in the transfer-INTO-tumour arm but not in this recovery arm, so proliferation over 7-13 days in an IL-15-replete host is unmeasured exactly where it is load-bearing. (4) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY worth recording: Results (line 54) say transfer into "untouched C57BL/6J mice" and readout at "7 days"; Methods say Ly5a x C57BL/6J recipients and "7 to 13 days." Evidence_types_all is otherwise correct and the G2 discipline on INF_TRAJECTORY (PAGA/diffusion pseudotime in PMID 38267402, hand-rooted in the Kaede-green cluster - I confirmed this at line 117 of R2_PMC10808449.txt) is properly applied. Excluding OBS_GENETIC was right: B2m CRISPR is on the tumour line, Prf1-/- is a functional knockout, neither is NK fate-mapping. IS IT A LINEAGE CLAIM: NO - upheld. R2 asks whether effector capacity can be restored, not whether A gives rise to B. The congenic marker is used to prove identity of the transferred population, not ancestry. It belongs with R1/R3.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: OBS_TRANSFER — but scope-limited, and weaker than the row conveys. The transfer observes only that congenically marked donor-derived NK cells recovered from a tumour-free host are functional 7-13 days later (PMID 39196934, Fig. 7 H-J, n = 10-15 recipient mice/group for function, n = 3-12 for ICPs). The step from that to "dysfunctional cells reverted" rests on fig. S7C, a cross-recipient population-frequency comparison, which is INF_KINETIC/INF_MARKER. Donor-level n is not reported and pooling is not stated, so the G5 unit is unresolved. Full list unchanged and correctly ordered: OBS_TRANSFER > INF_KINETIC > INF_INVITRO > INF_MARKER > INF_TRAJECTORY. No OBS_GENETIC, no OBS_DIRECT.
adv.new_counter_evidence: SIX ITEMS THE ROW MISSED, PLUS TWO CORRECTIONS TO ITS COUNTER-SOURCE. (1) GILL 2012, Blood 119:5758, PMID 22544698 — the NK-specific miss, and the most damaging. Adoptively transferred murine NK cells become exhausted; verbatim: "Loss of interferon (IFN)g production occurs early after transfer, whereas loss of cytotoxicity progresses with homeostatic proliferation and tumor exposure," and the state "can be partially reversed by the forced overexpression of Eomesodermin" — partially, and only by a genetic intervention. This destroys the tacit premise of the primary source's design, namely that 7-13 days of homeostatic proliferation in a tumour-free host is a neutral "rest period." In this paper homeostatic proliferation is itself a driver of NK functional change. Archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_G4gill_PMC3382935.txt (ABSTRACT_ONLY; JCI/Blood not in the EPMC OA subset). (2) DEAN 2024 INTERNAL COUNTER-EVIDENCE THE ROW DID NOT EXTRACT, from the row's own archived file /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PMC10808449.txt: line 61, verbatim — "Manipulation of TGFb, PGE2 or the transcription program controlled by HIF-1a, was insufficient to drive the full array of changes that define tumor-retained NK cells, implying that the coordinated action of multiple signals orchestrates this fate." That is peer-reviewed, in vivo, multi-model evidence directly undercutting the TGF-b-centric mechanistic premise of the row's chosen "fixed" counter-source. (3) ALSO FROM DEAN 2024, line 37: tumour-retained NK cells essentially do not leave the tumour — "The proportion and total number of KR+ NK cells in either tissue was very low, indicating that few NK cells egressed the tumor. Of those NK cells that did egress, the majority lacked CD49a expression." So the dysfunctional (CD49a+) cells stay put and the egressing ones are the not-yet-dysfunctional ones. The transfer-out design models a route that does not occur physiologically — a scope limitation stronger than the row's "splenic, not solid-tumour" point. (4) MERINO 2019 METHODS, PMID 31211698 — the row only ever had the abstract (archive /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PMC6715389.txt is status=ABSTRACT_ONLY). I recovered them from jci.org/articles/view/125916: Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChips, n = 7 donors, in vitro, CD3/CD19-depleted PBMC from HCMV-seropositive HEALTHY donors, 7 days plate-bound NKG2C agonist + IL-15, and — decisively — NO rest, withdrawal, or removal-of-stimulation experiment was performed. This cuts both ways and I report both: it means Merino cannot test reversibility, which UPHOLDS the row's narrow occupancy claim; but it also means the row's statement that the fixed arm has "exactly one strong dedicated primary study" understates it, because Merino is a second, peer-reviewed, primary, genome-wide methylation dataset establishing the fixed arm's premise (chronic stimulation reprograms NK epigenome concurrent with dysfunction). (5) SCOPE ERROR ON THE OCCUPANCY CLAIM: on the broader reading of "fixed," GAO 2017 Nat Immunol PMID 28759001 (with correction PMID 38514890) and CORTEZ 2017 Nat Immunol PMID 28759002 are peer-reviewed, in vivo, intratumoural, TGF-b-driven NK-to-ILC1 conversion — an irreversible-by-construction outcome. The screen already holds Gao under T1/T4 (/home/user/aaa/refs/T1_28759001.txt, T4_28759001.txt). The row's "fixed arm rests on one unrefereed preprint" is therefore true only under the narrow scoping "epigenetic fixation of NK dysfunction without identity change," and the row never states that scoping. Note the primary source explicitly EXCLUDED this axis in its own model (fig. S3E: no CD49a, Eomes-positive), which means primary and counter-source are testing NON-OVERLAPPING lesions and do not actually contradict each other. (6) COUNTER-SOURCE n VALUES THE ROW SAID DID NOT EXIST. The row states donor numbers for ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN and the HCC cohort "are not stated numerically anywhere in the preprint Methods." They are stated in the figure legends, which are present in the auditor's own sibling archive /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PPR1223917.txt: CUT&RUN n = 3 donors (line 137); HCC peripheral-blood ATAC-seq n = 3 (line 141); withdrawal-arm flow n = 7 donors, three independent experiments (line 125); intratumoural NK flow n = 10, LAMP1/IFN-g n = 12; xCELLigence killing 3 h n = 2, 24 h n = 7, 7 d n = 10. The row recovered figure-legend n for the primary source by exactly this route but did not do it for the counter-source. adv.crossfield_g4_findings: THE T-CELL EXHAUSTION FIELD HAS ALREADY RUN THIS EXACT EXPERIMENT AND REACHED THE OPPOSITE CONCLUSION. (A) PHILIP 2017, Nature 545:452, PMID 28514453 (full text archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_G4_PMC5693219.txt) is the decisive item and is the direct methodological template for PMID 39196934. Verbatim from the Results: "when we re-isolated TCR-TAG from liver lesions and cultured them in vitro with IL15... L5 and L7 regained the ability to produce IFNg and TNFa, but TCR-TAG isolated at day 12 and after did not. Thus state 1 dysfunction is plastic, but with further chromatin remodeling between days 7 and 14, becomes fixed (state 2)." Three consequences for R2. (i) REVERSIBILITY IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE STATE, IT IS A FUNCTION OF EXPOSURE DURATION. RMA-KR is a fast disseminated lymphoma; dysfunction appears within 16 h and mice are at end stage around days 12-14, so the sorted "late-stage" NK cells have had at most ~1-2 weeks of signal. In Philip's frame that samples the plastic window and cannot exclude a fixed state that the model never reaches. The claim as worded ("reversible versus fixed") is therefore likely a false dichotomy, and PMID 39196934 cannot resolve it because its model has no long-exposure arm. Strikingly, the counter-source preprint's own exposure is also 7 days — precisely the boundary. (ii) THE ICP RESULT IS NOT NOVEL AND THE ICP-LOSS READOUT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF REVERSION: "PD1 and LAG3 were similarly expressed by both plastic (L5, L7) and fixed (L14+) dysfunctional TST and thus not informative in this regard." PMID 39196934 uses loss of Lag-3/CD73/Tim-3 after transfer as part of its reversion evidence; the T-cell field established that those markers do not track the plastic/fixed axis. (iii) THE SELECTION ALTERNATIVE IS EMPIRICAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Philip sorted heterogeneous day-14 populations by CD38/CD101: "While CD38lo/CD101lo-L14 regained the ability to produce IFNg and TNFa, CD38hi/CD101hi-L14 did not." A bulk population that appears to revert can be reverting entirely in its plastic subfraction. PMID 39196934 transferred BULK sorted NK cells with no equivalent fractionation, so its result is fully compatible with a plastic subset recovering while a fixed subset does not. This converts the row's "SELECTION, NOT PER-CELL REVERSION" from speculation into a documented mechanism in the homologous system. (B) PAUKEN 2016, Science 354:1160, PMID 27789795 — exhaustion-specific chromatin is not remodelled by PD-1 blockade and reinvigoration is transient. A single-timepoint CD107a/IFN-g readout after rest, which is exactly what PMID 39196934 reports, is therefore not sufficient to establish that the underlying state reverted. The Sci Adv study performs no chromatin, methylation or ATAC readout at any point. (C) ABDEL-HAKEEM 2021, Nat Immunol 22:1008, PMID 34312545 (correction 34588688) — "Epigenetic scarring of exhausted T cells hinders memory differentiation upon eliminating chronic antigenic stimulation." This is the transfer-out logic executed properly: remove the chronic signal entirely, and epigenetic scars persist and block normal memory differentiation. Opposite outcome to R2's primary source, in the homologous system, with the chromatin readout R2's primary source lacks. (D) GHONEIM 2017, Cell 170:142, PMID 28648661 — de novo DNA methylation programs restrict PD-1-blockade-mediated rejuvenation; a functional rescue can coexist with an intact restrictive epigenome. (E) TRAINED IMMUNITY / MONOCYTE FIELD — a structural objection that applies to BOTH arms of R2 and that neither the row nor either source addresses. That field's central resolved question is where durable innate epigenetic memory is actually stored, and the answer is not the mature effector: human monocytes live ~5-7 days, far shorter than the years-long persistence of trained phenotypes, and the reservoir is long-lived bone-marrow HSPCs, with BCG-induced transcriptional/epigenetic remodelling demonstrated in the HSPC compartment and conveyed to peripheral CD14+ monocytes months later (Kaufmann 2018 Cell; Cirovic 2020 Cell Host Microbe; reviewed eLife 2025, PMID 40905954). Transplantation of sorted LT-HSCs alone was insufficient, implicating ST-HSC/MPP. Applied to R2: the entire reversible-versus-fixed dispute is being conducted on MATURE NK cells — mature splenic NK transferred for 7-13 days on the reversible side, mature healthy-donor NK in a 96-well plate for 17 days on the fixed side. Neither arm samples the compartment where the innate-memory field found durability to reside, and neither reports a route by which a mature-NK chromatin state would persist through turnover in vivo. That makes the fixed arm's in vitro ATAC signal of unestablished in vivo durability, and simultaneously makes the reversible arm's result less surprising than it is presented to be, since a mature short-lived effector's state is expected to be labile by construction. Whichever way R2 resolves, the experiment that would settle it — an NK progenitor/HSPC-level readout in tumour-bearing animals — has not been run by anyone. NOT SEARCHED in this pass: NK-cell-specific trained immunity (the Netea/Sun memory-NK literature) as a distinct sub-field; I searched monocyte/HSPC trained immunity only.

adv.better_primary_source: NO better primary source exists for the REVERSIBLE arm — PMID 39196934 (doi:10.1126/sciadv.adn0164, PMC11352832) is upheld, and the row's justification for preferring it over Ardolino 2014 (PMID 25329698) is sound: Ardolino treats while the tumour is still present and so cannot separate reinvigoration of dysfunctional cells from priming of not-yet-dysfunctional ones, a confound the Sci Adv introduction names explicitly (line 19: "it remains unclear if the beneficial effect of cytokines stemmed from priming NK cells that were not yet dysfunctional, from a genuine reinvigoration of dysfunctional cells, or from a bystander effect"). BUT THE COUNTER-SOURCE CHOICE SHOULD BE RESTRUCTURED, because the row anchors the entire "fixed" arm on a single unrefereed preprint when peer-reviewed anchors exist for its components: (a) PMID 31211698 (Merino 2019, JCI 129:3770, doi:10.1172/JCI125916) — peer-reviewed, primary, genome-wide EPIC-array methylation reprogramming in chronically stimulated human NK cells, n = 7 donors; it does NOT test withdrawal, so it establishes the fixed arm's premise but not its conclusion, and the row should carry it as such rather than having read only its abstract; (b) PMID 28759001 (Gao 2017, Nat Immunol) with correction PMID 38514890, and PMID 28759002 (Cortez 2017, Nat Immunol) — peer-reviewed, in vivo, intratumoural TGF-beta-driven NK-to-ILC1 conversion, i.e. a genuinely irreversible outcome, already archived in this screen under T1/T4; (c) PMID 22544698 (Gill 2012, Blood) — NK-specific, adoptive transfer, exhaustion progressing with homeostatic proliferation, only partially reversed by forced Eomes overexpression. AND THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE PAPER FOR ADJUDICATING R2 IS NOT AN NK PAPER AT ALL: PMID 28514453 (Philip 2017, Nature 545:452), which ran the identical remove-from-tumour-and-retest design in CD8 T cells, found reversibility to be a function of exposure duration (plastic to day 7, fixed from day 12-14), showed PD1/LAG3 do not discriminate the two states, and showed by CD38/CD101 sorting that apparent bulk reversion can come entirely from a plastic subfraction. It cannot serve as R2's primary source because it is not about NK cells, but no honest grading of R2 should omit it, and the row does. NET: primary source UPHELD; counter-source arm should be recorded as one unrefereed preprint (PPR1223917) PLUS PMID 31211698 for the epigenetic premise, with PMID 28514453 named as the cross-field template that both NK arms have failed to execute (no long-exposure arm on the reversible side, no tumour-derived cells on the fixed side).
